2.text: Anui camps led them to the fair. As late as 1879 Nordenskiöld saw several

3.text: dog-sledges passing by on their return from the fair, while during the whole

4.text: of my stay in the Kolyma district (1890-98), hardly a single dog-sledge came

5.text: to the fair from the maritime villages.

6.text: At the present time about six or seven hundred people gather together

7.text: for the Anui fair (Plate II, Figs. 1, 2). One-fourth of these are Russians,

8.text: Russianized natives, and Yakut, from settlements on the Anadyr, Kolyma,

9.text: Alaseya, and Indighirka; one-fourth are Kolyma Lamut; and the rest, Rein-

10.text: deer Chukchee and Kavraˊlɪt. Commerce has fallen off greatly, because American

11.text: peltries have nearly ceased to come, and part of the peltries from the Asiatic

12.text: shore are bought by the whalers. Of the remainder, a large portion goes to

13.text: the Anadyr. Of late the total of the Anui trade has been, according to official

14.text: data, from twenty to twenty-five thousand rubles annually. Of this amount,

15.text: two thirds is contributed by the Reindeer Chukchee; the remaining third belongs

16.text: to the Lamut, Russianized Yukaghir, etc.

17.text: OTHER FAIRS. — At about the time of the founding of the Anui fair, the

18.text: Anadyr and the Telqäˊp Chukchee began to trade at Gishiginsk and Kamen-

19.text: skoye, on the Sea of Okhotsk. In the beginning of the century, simultaneously

20.text: with a spring fair for the Reindeer Koryak, was established another one for

21.text: the southwestern Chukchee on the Parapolsky Dol, not far from the upper

22.text: part of the river Opuka. In the village of Markova, on the Middle Anadyr,

23.text: a fair was held, for the Anadyr and Oˊnmɪlɪn Chukchee. During the last

24.text: fifteen years, from the time of the institution of separate district administration

25.text: in Anadyr, three more fairs were opened, — one, the Tumanskaya fair, on

26.text: the west (Plate III, Fig. 1), near the mountain Iˊrg̣u-ñei (“pointed mountain”),
26.note: abraded hyphen. there are NO middle dots in this text as far as i'm aware

27.text: chiefly for the Telqäˊp Chukchee; another in the small village of Vaˊkarena,

28.text: on the Middle Anadyr, for the Oˊnmɪlɪn; and a third on the Yeropol River,

29.text: for the Chukchee of the Upper Anadyr and for the Lamut (Plate III, Fig. 2).

30.text: The extent of trade in the Anadyr region, however, is by no means sufficient

31.text: to support all these fairs, the annual receipts being about twenty thousand

32.text: rubles. In 1901, on account of heavy snows, only two Telqäˊp camps went

33.text: to the Tumanskaya fair, and but three Oˊnmɪlɪn camps to the Vaˊkarena.

34.text: The annual trade at the Chukchee fair on the Opuka River amounts to not

35.text: more than a few thousand rubles.

36.text: ROUTES. — In former times a few Russian traders went with dog-sledges

37.text: along the seashore from the mouth of the Kolyma to the Arctic villages. This

38.text: route was shorter, but more difficult, than the inland one, because between the

39.text: mouth of the Kolyma and Cape Erri there are no settlements whatsoever. The

40.text: last of these traders was the Cossack, Ivan Kudrin, who, in 1882, brought W. H.

41.text: Gilder to the Kolyma, and in a way wanted to take him captive, as Mr. Gilder
